$comment: Best known value for every non-demo hill-climb task, by mission and task id. Full points are paid only for beating these. See docs/BEST-KNOWN.md. Checked by scripts/check-best-known.py in CI.

minimize_total_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox/aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103-gd32-xx71-10.circ.txt: 103 gates (32 AND, 61 XOR, 10 XNOR), added 29 Oct 2026. Earlier: S. Jain (Oct 2026 preprint) 106; NIST 110; Boyar-Peralta/Calik 113.
minimize_total_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26. The live Sunstead record of 103 (codex-dirichlet, 25 Nov 2026) is gate-for-gate this circuit, so it ties best_known.

minimize_and_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox/aes-sbox-a28-ad5-g128-gd20-xx100-27.circ.txt (28 AND, 128 gates) and 32 other 28-AND circuits. Boyar-Peralta's 32 AND is no longer the best known.
minimize_and_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

capset_f3_4.source: G. Pellegrino (1970): maximum cap set size in AG(4, 3) = F_3^4 is exactly 20 (OEIS A090245).

capset_f3_5.source: Y. Edel, S. Ferret, I. Landjev, L. Storme, 'The classification of the largest caps in AG(5, 3)', J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 99 (2002): maximum cap set in F_3^5 is exactly 45 (OEIS A090245).

capset_f3_6.source: A. Potechin, 'Maximal caps in AG(6, 3)', Des. Codes Cryptogr. 46 (2008), arXiv:0802.0789: maximum cap set in F_3^6 is exactly 112 (OEIS A090245).

capset_f3_7.source: Y. Edel, 'Extensions of generalized product caps', Des. Codes Cryptogr. 31 (2004): largest known cap set in F_3^7 has size 236 (open frontier; upper bound 276; OEIS A090245).

ap3_n64.source: OEIS A003002 (b003002.txt) / J. Dybizbanski, Electron. J. Combin. 19(2) (2012): exact value r_3(64) = 20.

ap3_n100.source: OEIS A003002 (b003002.txt) / J. Dybizbanski, Electron. J. Combin. 19(2) (2012): exact value r_3(100) = 27.

ap3_n150.source: OEIS A003002 (b003002.txt) / J. Dybizbanski, Electron. J. Combin. 19(2) (2012): exact value r_3(150) = 35.

ap3_n200.source: OEIS A003002 (b003002.txt): exact value r_3(200) = 41 (verified through n = 211).

ap3_n300.source: Derived from OEIS A003002 exact r_3(100) = 27: for any 27-element 3-AP-free set A in {0..99}, A union (A + 200) in {0..299} has size 54 and is 3-AP-free because any cross-interval midpoint lies in [100, 199].
ap3_n300.note: Exact r_3(300) is open; replace with a stronger literature lower bound if published.

sidon_n100.source: Exact equivalence to Optimal Golomb Rulers (OEIS A003022): G(12) = 85 <= 99 < 106 = G(13), so the largest Sidon set in {0..99} has exactly 12 elements.

sidon_n150.source: Exact equivalence to Optimal Golomb Rulers (OEIS A003022): G(14) = 127 <= 149 < 151 = G(15), so the largest Sidon set in {0..149} has exactly 14 elements.

sidon_n200.source: Exact equivalence to Optimal Golomb Rulers (OEIS A003022): G(17) = 199 <= 199 < 216 = G(18), so the largest Sidon set in {0..199} has exactly 17 elements.

sidon_n300.source: Exact equivalence to Optimal Golomb Rulers (OEIS A003022): G(20) = 283 <= 299 < 333 = G(21), so the largest Sidon set in {0..299} has exactly 20 elements.

sidon_n500.source: Exact equivalence to Optimal Golomb Rulers (OEIS A003022): G(26) = 492 <= 499 < 553 = G(27), so the largest Sidon set in {0..499} has exactly 26 elements.

ca_2_15_3.source: C. J. Colbourn, Covering Array Tables (CAN(2, 15, 3) <= 15); also benchmarked in Wu, Nie, Kuo, Leung, Colbourn, IEEE TEVC 19(4) (2015).

ca_2_20_3.source: C. J. Colbourn, Covering Array Tables (CAN(2, 20, 3) <= 15); also benchmarked in Wu, Nie, Kuo, Leung, Colbourn, IEEE TEVC 19(4) (2015).

ca_2_15_4.source: C. J. Colbourn, Covering Array Tables (CAN(2, 15, 4) <= 24); also benchmarked in Wu, Nie, Kuo, Leung, Colbourn, IEEE TEVC 19(4) (2015).

ca_2_20_4.source: C. J. Colbourn, Covering Array Tables (CAN(2, 20, 4) <= 28); also benchmarked in Wu, Nie, Kuo, Leung, Colbourn, IEEE TEVC 19(4) (2015).

ca_3_12_2.source: Exact value CAN(3, 12, 2) = 15 (Nurmela / Colbourn Covering Array Tables; proven no 14-row strength-3 binary CA on 12 columns exists).

ca_3_16_2.source: Exact value CAN(3, 16, 2) = 17 (Colbourn Covering Array Tables; proven optimal by exact classification of strength-3 binary covering arrays).

ca_3_20_2.source: Exact value CAN(3, 20, 2) = 18 (Sloane / Roux / Colbourn Covering Array Tables; proven optimal for 17 <= k <= 20).

sm4_linear_l_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count found on 2026-11-26. Floor from a stock randomized Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py, deterministic, about a minute); it matches the hand construction a = t^rotl8(t), b = a^rotl16(t), L = rotl2(b)^rotl24(a).
sm4_linear_l_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

sm4_key_lprime_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count found on 2026-11-26, and the stock Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py) finds nothing below the seed (the three rotation pairs share no common pair). Any strict improvement is treated as new.
sm4_key_lprime_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

aria_diffusion_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count for the 16x16 binary ARIA matrix was confirmed on 2026-11-26 (the mission text's '36' is unsourced). Floor from the stock Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py).
aria_diffusion_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

camellia_p_xor.source: 16 XORs, held by the live Sunstead record (codex-dirichlet, re-checked 2026-11-26). Believed to equal the Camellia designers' cost for the P-function (Aoki et al., 'Camellia: A 128-Bit Block Cipher Suitable for Multiple Platforms', SAC 2000); the stock Paar heuristic only reaches 20.
camellia_p_xor.note: The designers' figure has not been confirmed from the paper text yet.

clyde128_lbox_xor.source: D. Bellizia et al. (Spook/Clyde-128, ToSC 2020) / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-spook.c: 12 32-bit word XORs = 384 bit-XORs (stock randomized Paar on the expanded 64x64 matrix reaches 580).

ascon_sigma0_xor.source: NIST SP 800-232 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-ascon.c: two 64-bit word XORs = 128 bit-XORs; stock randomized Paar (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py, 15 runs, seed 1) finds no reduction below 128.

ascon_sigma2_xor.source: NIST SP 800-232 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-ascon.c: two 64-bit word XORs = 128 bit-XORs; stock randomized Paar (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py, 15 runs, seed 1) finds no reduction below 128.

skinny8_total_gates.source: C. Beierle et al., 'The SKINNY Family of Block Ciphers and Its Low-Latency Variant MANTIS', CRYPTO 2016 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-skinnyutil.h: 8 NOR + 8 XOR maps to 8 NOT + 8 AND + 8 XNOR = 24 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not}.

skinny8_and_gates.source: C. Beierle et al., CRYPTO 2016 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-skinnyutil.h: defining 4-round SKINNY-128 S-box uses exactly 8 NOR/AND gates.

skinny8_and_depth.source: C. Beierle et al., CRYPTO 2016 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-skinnyutil.h: defining 4-round iterated NOR-XOR SKINNY-128 S-box has AND-depth 4 (algebraic degree 6 gives theoretical lower bound 3).

ascon_total_gates.source: NIST SP 800-232 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-ascon.c bitsliced 5-bit Ascon S-box: 5 AND + 5 NOT + 10 XOR + 1 XNOR = 21 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not}.

ascon_and_gates.source: C. Dobraunig, M. Eichlseder, F. Mendel, M. Schlaffer (Ascon / NIST SP 800-232) and K. Stoffelen (ePrint 2016/198): 5-bit quadratic Ascon S-box has optimal multiplicative complexity 5.

keccak_chi_total_gates.source: G. Bertoni, J. Daemen, M. Peeters, G. Van Assche (NIST FIPS 202) / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-keccak.c: 5-bit Keccak chi uses 5 NOT + 5 AND + 5 XOR = 15 gates.

present_total_gates.source: N. Courtois, D. Hulme, T. Mourouzis (2011) and K. Stoffelen, 'Optimizing S-box Implementations for Several Criteria using SAT Solvers', FSE 2016 (ePrint 2016/198): 14 gates for PRESENT S-box in {xor, xnor, and, not}.

present_and_gates.source: K. Stoffelen, FSE 2016 (ePrint 2016/198): PRESENT 4-bit S-box has optimal multiplicative complexity 4.

gift_total_gates.source: S. Banik et al., 'GIFT: A Small Present', CHES 2017 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-gift128.c: 4 AND + 4 XOR + 2 XNOR + 2 NOT = 12 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not}.

gift_and_gates.source: S. Banik et al., CHES 2017 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-gift128.c: GIFT 4-bit S-box has optimal multiplicative complexity 4.

spongent_total_gates.source: K. Stoffelen, FSE 2016 (ePrint 2016/198): SAT-optimized 4-bit SPONGENT S-box implementation achieves 14 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not} (rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-spongent.c uses 18 gates).

spongent_and_gates.source: A. Bogdanov et al. (SPONGENT, CHES 2011) / K. Stoffelen (ePrint 2016/198): SPONGENT 4-bit S-box has optimal multiplicative complexity 4.

saturnin_total_gates.source: A. Canteaut et al., 'Saturnin: a suite of lightweight symmetric algorithms for post-quantum security', ToSC 2020 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-saturnin.c: 6-stage bitsliced 4-bit S-box circuit.

knot_total_gates.source: W. Zhang et al. (KNOT NIST LWC submission) / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-knot.c: 4 nonlinear + 6 XOR + NOT gates = 14 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not}.

clyde_total_gates.source: D. Bellizia et al., 'Spook: Sponge-Based Leakage-Resistant Authenticated Encryption with a Masked Tweakable Block Cipher', ToSC 2020 / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-spook.c: 4 AND + 4 XOR = 8 gates.

pyjamask_total_gates.source: D. Goudarzi et al. (Pyjamask NIST LWC submission) / rweather/lightweight-crypto internal-pyjamask.c: 4 AND + 7 XOR + 1 NOT = 12 gates in {xor, xnor, and, not} (final 3-XOR swap is wire relabeling).

sm4_total_gates.source: No published gate count for this S-box in the {xor, xnor, and, not} basis was found on 2026-11-26. It is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion, like the AES S-box, so the AES S-box best known (103, NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103) is used as a conservative proxy: anything below it is a strong result.
sm4_total_gates.note: Replace with a sourced SM4 S-box circuit count when one is found.

sm4_and_gates.source: Every S-box here is affine-equivalent to inversion in GF(2^8) (CryptoSbox/Spec.lean proves the algebraic definitions). Composing a circuit for the AES S-box with the right affine maps costs no AND gates, so the NIST 28-AND AES circuits (usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox, a28) give 28 here too.

aes_inv_total_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-invsbox/aes-invsbox-a32-ad7-g105-gd27-xx73-14.circ.txt: 105 gates (32 AND, 59 XOR, 14 XNOR). Earlier: S. Jain (Oct 2026 preprint) 109; NIST 112.
aes_inv_total_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

aes_inv_and_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-invsbox/aes-invsbox-a28-ad5-g126-gd27-xx98-26.circ.txt (28 AND, 126 gates).
aes_inv_and_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

It is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion, like the AES S-box, so the AES S-box best known (103, NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103) is used as a conservative proxy: anything below it is a strong result.
camellia_total_gates.note: Replace with a sourced Camellia S-box circuit count when one is found.

camellia_and_gates.source: Every S-box here is affine-equivalent to inversion in GF(2^8) (CryptoSbox/Spec.lean proves the algebraic definitions). Composing a circuit for the AES S-box with the right affine maps costs no AND gates, so the NIST 28-AND AES circuits (usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox, a28) give 28 here too.

whirlpool_total_gates.source: No published {xor, xnor, and, not} total gate count for Whirlpool's 8-bit mini-box S-box was confirmed on 2026-11-26; NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103 (103 gates) is used as a conservative 8-bit degree-7 S-box proxy.
whirlpool_total_gates.note: Replace with a sourced Whirlpool S-box circuit count when confirmed (mini-box decompositions may go lower).

whirlpool_and_gates.source: No published multiplicative complexity for Whirlpool's 8-bit S-box was confirmed on 2026-11-26; NIST usnistgov/Circuits 28-AND AES S-box is used as a conservative proxy (Whirlpool's five 4-bit mini-boxes may reach ~20-24 AND gates).
whirlpool_and_gates.note: Replace with a sourced Whirlpool multiplicative complexity bound when confirmed.

whirlpool_and_depth.source: No published minimum AND-depth for Whirlpool's 8-bit degree-7 S-box was confirmed on 2026-11-26; depth 4 (NIST usnistgov/Circuits AES depth-4 family) is used as a conservative proxy (algebraic degree 7 gives lower bound 3; seed mini-box layering has depth 6).

aria_s2_total_gates.source: ARIA S2 (RFC 5794) is affine-equivalent to x -> x^247 = (x^-1)^8 over GF(2^8), which is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion because x -> x^8 is F2-linear; NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103 (103 gates) is used as a conservative proxy.

aria_s2_and_gates.source: ARIA S2 is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion (x^247 = (x^-1)^8 and x^8 is F2-linear). Composing NIST usnistgov/Circuits 28-AND AES S-box circuits with linear pre/post-maps costs 0 AND gates, giving 28.

aria_s2_and_depth.source: ARIA S2 is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion (algebraic degree 7 => lower bound ceil(log2 7) = 3). Composing NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a35-ad3-g139 (AND-depth 3) with linear maps achieves optimal AND-depth 3.

aria_invs2_total_gates.source: ARIA InvS2 (RFC 5794) is the inverse of ARIA S2 and hence affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion; NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a32-ad7-g103 (103 gates) is used as a conservative proxy.

aria_invs2_and_gates.source: ARIA InvS2 is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion. Composing NIST usnistgov/Circuits 28-AND AES S-box circuits with linear pre/post-maps costs 0 AND gates, giving 28.

aria_invs2_and_depth.source: ARIA InvS2 is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion (algebraic degree 7 => lower bound 3). Composing NIST usnistgov/Circuits aes-sbox-a35-ad3-g139 (AND-depth 3) with linear maps achieves optimal AND-depth 3.

goldilocks_inv.source: Verified constructive runs addition chain for Goldilocks p-2 = 2^64 - 2^32 - 1 = (2^32 - 2)*2^32 + (2^32 - 1) using the 37-step chain for 2^31 - 1 (l(31)=7), taking 72 operations total.

goldilocks_inv_d7.source: Plonky3/Plonky3@0d803737b6 field/src/exponentiation.rs (exp_10540996611094048183): 63 squares + 8 multiplications = 71 operations total.

babybear_inv.source: Verified constructive factored addition chain for BabyBear p-2 = 0x77ffffff = 17 * 0x070f0f0f (33 steps for 0x070f0f0f + 5 steps to multiply by 17 = 2^4 + 1), taking 38 operations total.

babybear_inv_d7.source: Plonky3/Plonky3@0d803737b6 field/src/exponentiation.rs (exp_1725656503): 29 squares + 8 multiplications = 37 operations total.

koalabear_inv.source: Verified constructive runs addition chain for KoalaBear p-2 = 0x7effffff (6 ones, 0, four 6-bit blocks of ones using 2^6 - 1 in 8 steps), taking 37 operations total.

koalabear_inv_d3.source: Plonky3/Plonky3@0d803737b6 field/src/exponentiation.rs (exp_1420470955): 29 squares + 7 multiplications = 36 operations total.

mersenne31_inv.source: Verified constructive runs addition chain for Mersenne31 p-2 = 2^31 - 3 = ((2^29 - 1) << 2) + 1 using l(29)=7 (35 steps for 2^29 - 1 + 2 doubles + 1 add), taking 38 operations total.

mersenne31_inv_d5.source: Plonky3/Plonky3@0d803737b6 field/src/exponentiation.rs (exp_1717986917): 30 squares + 7 multiplications = 37 operations total.

bn254_inv.source: Stock 5-bit sliding-window addition chain for BN254 p-2 (254-bit prime), verified at 309 operations total (Plonky3 uses gcd inversion for BN254).
bn254_inv.note: Replace with an addchain/continued-fraction optimal bound (~295) when verified.

bn254_inv_d5.source: Stock 5-bit sliding-window addition chain for BN254 1/5 mod (p-1), verified at 309 operations total.
bn254_inv_d5.note: Replace with an addchain/continued-fraction optimal bound (~295) when verified.
